case_title: KALICHARAN & ORS. v. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.307; Arms Act s.25
trial_court_outcome: Convicted for offences punishable under Sections 148, 302, 307 of IPC and Section 25 of Arms Act
neutral_facts: The prosecution case is that on 6th December 2000, the informant was carrying soil for levelling a lane by his bullock cart. When he reached near the house of the accused, he was resisted and forced to turn back his bullock cart. There was an altercation between the accused and the informant. The accused went back to their house and came back with weapons. It was alleged that the accused fired shots from a pistol, which hit the deceased and caused his death. The prosecution mainly relied upon the evidence of eyewitnesses who were allegedly injured at the hands of the accused. The evidence of the prosecution witnesses and the post-mortem report indicated that the deceased suffered injuries caused by sharp weapons, not bullet injuries. The charge framed by the trial court alleged that the deceased died due to bullet injuries sustained from the accused's pistol, but the evidence did not support this. The accused were not informed of the actual circumstances of the deceased's death, which led to a failure in the trial process.
